observations.title: First-create uniqueness recovery skips requested-type binding
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata
observations.counterevidence: Ordinary existing rows reject mismatches; only uniqueness conflicts are recovered; disabled rows are checked after both branches. The existing concurrency test only supplies a SIMPLE request and SIMPLE winner.
observations.nextPublicSeam: In GeneratorFactoryTest call public nextResult with a SIMPLE request, stub initial select=null, insert=DuplicateKeyException, reread=DATABASE winner; assert SEQ006 and no generator/history calls. Repeat through batchResult. Lead can extend/run this existing test; nothing was executed here.
observations.cause: A null lookup enters the create branch. DuplicateKeyException rereads/caches the winning row at 308–317 but never runs the requested/existing-type comparison at 321–326. Two different-type first callers can follow the winner instead of the losing caller receiving SEQ006; nextResult dispatches the resulting type.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Actual uniqueness constraint/transaction visibility and simultaneous DB callers. No claim of duplicate generated IDs.

observations.title: DATABASE batch loop cannot terminate normally at signed-long maximum
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata
observations.counterevidence: Ordinary returned maxima terminate; initialization attempts are bounded. The mapper may reject overflow/exhaustion, but its SQL was not read.
observations.nextPublicSeam: Mock the mapper to return Long.MAX_VALUE for public batch("orders",1); exercise in an isolated fork with a hard process deadline, not an indefinitely running in-process test. Assert a finite one-value result or a defined exhaustion exception after a bounded implementation. Lead owns creating/running this test.
observations.cause: If incrementAndGet returns Long.MAX_VALUE, the inclusive `long v <= max; v++` loop wraps v to Long.MIN_VALUE. All signed long values satisfy v<=Long.MAX_VALUE, so normal termination is impossible; allocation failure/interruption of the process may intervene.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Reachability in real DB, JDBC/SQL overflow behavior, memory impact. No live exhaustion attempt was made.
observations.requirementText: [atomic sequence increment contract](<../../CODING_GUIDE.md#L67-L71>) and the bounded returned batch contract at [85–109](<../../../astral-sequence/src/main/java/com/astral/sequence/generator/DatabaseGenerator.java#L85-L109>).

observations.title: API metric cardinality threshold does not bound concrete URI keys
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata
observations.counterevidence: Platform whitelist, URI length limit, existing-key fast path and periodic drain reduce costs but do not bound URI cardinality. This is a local map-bound failure, not a demonstrated anonymous HTTP attack.
observations.nextPublicSeam: Call public ApiMetricCollector.record with 20,001+ distinct valid `/api/v1/.../id-N` URIs, fixed method/status/platform and empty version; drain and count keys. Separately pass a matched-template request through public interceptor afterCompletion to capture its supplied URI. No network needed.
observations.cause: The caller passes normalized raw requestURI, not the matched route template. On threshold exhaustion the collector only empties appVersion; computeIfAbsent still inserts every distinct URI. Distinct path IDs can create >20,000 keys even with empty version.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Reachable variable-ID routes, ingress controls, traffic volume and heap impact.

observations.title: Whitelisted PATCH-style updates still overwrite omitted concurrent changes
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata

Assert omitted fields are absent from SET or conflict is explicit; later verify real isolation through Lead's authorized test lane.
observations.cause: Null/omitted fields are resolved from the earlier selected row and then unconditionally included in wrapper SET. An omitted enabled field can overwrite a toggle committed after the read. Whitelisting columns prevents mass assignment, not stale values within the whitelist.

observations.title: Config cache eviction precedes transactional commit
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata

observations.cause: update calls evictConfigCache before returning from its transactional method. A separate reader between eviction and proxy commit could reload the previous committed row, which then remains cached for up to 60 seconds.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Proxy transaction boundary, isolation and the actual interleaving; no unconditional stale-disabled issuance claim.

observations.title: Async stats success acknowledgment cannot communicate processing drops
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata
observations.counterevidence: Best-effort telemetry may intentionally permit loss; admission rate limits and batch bound reduce load. Executor submission rejection could still throw before success, but does not communicate later semaphore/processing outcomes.
observations.nextPublicSeam: Use the actual proxied ingestion service with blocked harmless mapper stubs to occupy admission permits, call public report for the extra batch, capture Result and processed count. Decide/document best-effort acceptance or require explicit admission failure before acknowledging.
observations.cause: The controller calls a void async method and returns success. Semaphore rejection returns/drops inside that method; processing exceptions are caught there. Those outcomes cannot become the caller's failure acknowledgment, contrary to the nearby client-retry/no-loss rationale.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Originating durability/retry requirement, actual proxy/executor saturation and client retry logic. No promise of exactly-once ingestion is assumed.

observations.title: Snowflake deployment uniqueness and bounded clock waiting remain unproven
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata
observations.counterevidence: Deployment may allocate distinct nodes; typical clock advancement ends the spin quickly; >10ms observed rollback throws and range checks fail fast. Cross-key equality is **not** a defect without a global-uniqueness requirement.
observations.nextPublicSeam: Lead verifies actual node allocation contract, then exercises public next on two instances under a controlled clock through a narrow production-shared clock seam; test sequence-wrap with a fixed clock using an isolated hard deadline. No private-state-only proof of production uniqueness.
observations.cause: Valid range is not unique allocation across instances; defaults reuse node1/datacenter1. Sequence wrap waits for wall clock advancement without deadline/interruption handling while holding the key lock. Timestamp assembly contains no bizKey, so cross-key numerical equality is possible, but per-key uniqueness is the visible design.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Deployment node assignment, frozen/adjusted clocks, restart persistence, epoch exhaustion and globally unique-ID requirement.

observations.title: Optional resource probe timeout does not cancel/bound underlying tasks
observations.changeContext: Current working-tree observation; introduction by WIP not established from file-level metadata
observations.counterevidence: Real clients/pools may impose finite timeouts; virtual threads are cheaper; completed probes release connections. Missing resources return without a task. A bounded caller wait is a real positive, not cancellation.
observations.nextPublicSeam: Supply blocking fake DataSource/RedisConnectionFactory to public getDatabaseInfo/getRedisInfo; issue repeated calls beyond3s, count outstanding fake acquisitions/tasks, release all latches in finally, and assert a chosen admission/cancellation bound. No real DB/Redis.
observations.cause: Each call starts a new virtual-thread probe. get(3s) times out only the waiting caller; the future is not retained/cancelled and no admission bound is visible. Slow underlying acquisition/queries can accumulate probes under polling. Both static executors have no visible destruction hook.
observations.untestedBoundaries: Driver cancellation/timeout behavior, active-task accumulation and deployment poll rate.
